name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_SelectOffsetItem
signature: void maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_SelectOffsetItem(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 offset)

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollGrid_MoveCursor
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollGrid_MoveCursor(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int pageCount)

name: Ui_Window_EnsureEntrySelected
summary: Small helper: ensures the current entry is visible, then selects the entry encoded in the high half of f_98 on the bound list.
evidence: The 28-byte body is fully readable: Ui_ListWindow_EnsureEntryVisible, then vtable+0x58 and Ui_List_SelectEntryById with f_98<<16.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_AdvanceScrollPage
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_AdvanceScrollPage(Ui_ListWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int page)
summary: Scroll helper of a list window: forwards to Ui_ScrollList_ScrollBy and, when the entry count plus the stored page times five reaches the visible-row count, commits the new scroll offset through the window vtable and updates the stored page word.
evidence: Ui_ScrollList_ScrollBy and Ui_List_SelectEntryById are named and the vtable+0x68 visible-row call plus the page*5 arithmetic are visible, but there are no callers to disambiguate the window class.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemList_ScrollToIndex
summary: Moves an item list to the page containing the current index: converts the index to page/row with divide-by-12, writes the row through the list model, stores the page at self[0x13] and clamps to the 11/12-row range.
evidence: The divide-by-12 magic 0x2AAAAAAB, the vtable+0x64 count / +0x68 visible-row calls and the two pager writes match the sibling 0x003E5EA4, but there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollClampRows12
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_ScrollClampRows12(void* list, int (*getCount)(int), u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int cursor, int max)
summary: Thumb scroll clamp for a 12-row list: compares the cursor row against the row count, derives the page with divide-by-12, clamps the scroll offset into the 11/12-row window, re-selects the entry and refreshes the scroll bar.
evidence: The divide-by-12 and 0xB/0xC clamps are visible, but two row values come from unaff_r5/unaff_r6 and the function sits in an unreferenced Thumb fragment block.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByDeltaThumb
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByDeltaThumb(void* list, int delta, u32 arg3, int listHandle)
summary: Thumb scroll-by-delta step for a 12-row list window: adds delta to the stored row, clamps the offset into the 11/12-row window, re-selects and refreshes the list.
evidence: The delta add and divide-by-12 clamp are readable, but the second half runs on a shifted row used as a pointer and the function ends in halt_baddata; it is an unreferenced Thumb fragment.

name: Ui_Window_SelectEntryC
summary: Fetches the bound list through vtable+0x58 and selects the entry id stored at self+0x28 (high-half encoding); third identical copy of the same three-operation body.
evidence: The 52-byte body is fully readable and identical to 0x002D888C/0x00214A78: vtable+0x58 then Ui_List_SelectEntryById with *(u16*)(window+0x28)<<16.

name: maybe_Ui_Row_Activate
summary: Clears the selected bit on two child icons, sets it on the third, re-selects the row's entry id, then re-measures the text and re-applies the row.
evidence: The icon bit updates on three children plus Ui_List_SelectEntryById and maybe_Ui_Row_Apply are visible, but the Thumb frame is damaged (unaff_r5/unaff_r11) and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_SelectEntryByCursor
summary: Selects the entry under the list cursor: fetches the bound list (vtable+0x58) and selects row (self[0x14]-1) with the window id in the high half.
evidence: Only the trailing vtable+0x58 select is readable; the prologue is lost (unaff_r4/r5/r6, in_CY, halt_baddata) and the callee list (std_destroy_range, Ui_Object_DtorBase) does not match the visible body.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByPageThumbA
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByPageThumbA(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, UiListWidget* list)
summary: Thumb page-scroll step of a five-row list: recomputes the selected entry from the visible-row count and page*5, selects it and refreshes the window.
evidence: The body uses unaff_r7/unaff_r8 for the page and the stored page, and the 0x6E5xxx block is unreferenced Thumb fragments; only the select/refresh sequence is reliable.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByPageThumbB
summary: Four-call Thumb fragment of a list scroll step: select entry, visible-row getter (vtable+0x64), scroll setter and window refresh.
evidence: All arguments are missing (unaff_r4, calls with no parameters) and the function is a mid-function fragment, so only the four-call shape is known.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByPageThumbC
summary: Third Thumb page-scroll fragment: clamps the target row to the 11/12-row range, sets the scroll position, re-selects the entry and refreshes the window.
evidence: All arguments are lost (unaff_r4/r5/r7/r8, undefined arg2/arg5/arg6), the jump table is unrecovered and the address is unreferenced.

summary: State handler of the message panel: honours the pending flags at +0x2048, looks up the queued message id and emits opcode 3 or opcode 2 with argument 2, pushing the matching pane.

name: Ui_Message_SetNameArg

name: maybe_Message_SetArgTextPair
summary: Installs one text argument and two label strings into the message-argument store (argument 5 plus the two 0x00707C1C label slots) and clears the 0x40-byte scratch block.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_CreateActionPane
summary: Creates the battle action panes: makes an action-animation entry, initialises the action panes with Ui_ActionPane_Init and installs them into slots through Container_SlotReplace.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PushActionBlockedMessage
summary: For the actor at actorIndex: plays SE 0xA6B, sets the actor's display state and pushes a battle message row built from the actor record's f_52/f_54 message ids; when the helper 0x0048ECE8 reports the actor ineligible it clears the popups and replays popup 0x4B.
evidence: Both callers are now confident (Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchCommand, Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessActorCommand) and the body definitely pushes a message row, but 'blocked' still depends on the unnamed helper 0x0048ECE8.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchActorEvent
summary: For the current actor (vtable +0x60): counts in self[0x377C] when the battle flag +0x4244 is set; when the actor fails four checks (vtable +0x10, Item_Container_CanAddItem, accepted types 8 and 10) it clears the popups and spawns popup 0x636, otherwise it calls Battle_SelectActionTargets.
evidence: Both callers are confident (Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchCommand, Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessActorCommand) and the gate plus popup 0x636 are visible, but the body also calls Battle_SelectActionTargets and shows no event dispatch, so the noun remains the first pass's guess.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessStatusCommand
summary: Status-effect command branch: if the actor carries effect id 0xD/0xE/0xF it records self+0xDE0A = 1 and clears those effects; otherwise it shows balloon 0xF and replays popup 0x4B.
evidence: The only caller is Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchCommand and the body tests unit vt[0xE8] for effect ids 0xD/0xE/0xF before setting self+0xDE0A, which is exactly the status-effect command branch.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PushActorStateMessage
summary: Posts one popup message for the current actor: id 0x4B when the actor state is 9, otherwise the literal id at 0x003C4AAC, handed to Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair as an {actor, index, id} descriptor.
evidence: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair is now named, which confirms the popup-queue role, but both ids are unnamed literals and the tail is a bogus call followed by halt_baddata.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateState29DD
summary: Battle UI state machine stage (state base 0x29DD): shows or hides the target marker rows, advances by 0x0F/0x16 and either queues the action or posts a message.
evidence: Battle_Ui_ForwardCommand and Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty are confident and the state comparison against g_480ED4 (0x29DD) is explicit, but the name only encodes a state id and says nothing about behaviour.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateState2A9D
summary: State handler for state base 0x2A9D: alternates between the 0x0E and 0x16 sub-states, updates the row visibility flags and returns a boolean.
evidence: Battle_Model_ApplyMonsterSize and Battle_Ui_ForwardCommand are confident neighbours and the state base is explicit, but the name only encodes the state id.

summary: Composite actor-action updater (fourth variant): runs the action's sub-steps, stores the sub-index at +0x1308 and returns the second done flag at +0xD3.

evidence: The address range 0x47F9AA..0x47F9FC lies inside 0x47F794 (length 0x216) and starts in Thumb mode while the parent is ARM, so it is a decompiler artefact rather than a callable entry point.

evidence: The 72-byte body is fully readable: Anim_ModelInstance_Release, std_destroy_range(child+0x50, 0x005646E4, 0x14, 2), free and a zero store at +8 - identical to the cleanup branch of 0x003D15C4.

name: maybe_Battle_Manager_UpdateCommandState
summary: Per-frame state machine advancing battle command/target selection, driving the target markers and the window-idle checks.
evidence: Neighbours Ui_BattleTargetMarker_UpdatePositions/ReleaseAll/CreateFromModelId, Ui_Window_IsGroupIdle and Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor are named, but the state ids 0xFFB..0x1020 are unnamed and there are no callers.
